card: This pull request integrates Schnorr signature batch verification into block validation using an experimental secp256k1 batch module. Currently, Schnorr signatures are verified individually per transaction input, missing significant CPU speedups available through batch verification. Benchmarks committed with the secp256k1 module indicate large verification speedups over single signature checks. The change depends on upstream secp256k1 PRs 1134 and 1789, which are not yet merged.
evidence: secp256k1 benchmark data and speedup plots included in the PR commit (secp256k1/doc/speedup-batch.md, bench_output.txt) show substantial throughput speedup of Schnorr batch verification over single verification.
The PR author states the draft is opened for 'conceptual discussion, and collaborative benchmarking' while the underlying secp256k1 batch module (secp256k1#1134) remains under review.
problem: Schnorr signatures in Taproot transactions are currently verified individually during block validation. Validating each signature separately misses the mathematical performance gains of batch verification supported by BIP 340.
scope_notes: A significant portion of the diff consists of vendored secp256k1 code from upstream pull requests (secp256k1#1134 and secp256k1#1789) that are not yet merged in libsecp256k1. In Bitcoin Core, it refactors CCheckQueue and validation script-checking types.
summary: Vendors an experimental batch verification module in secp256k1 and integrates Schnorr signature batch verification into block validation. It introduces a collecting signature checker and batchable script checks that aggregate Schnorr signatures across inputs and verify them together in both parallel and single-threaded check queues.
